followup_explanation:
I picked Dunlin for a few concrete reasons:

1. **It's the stronger general model.** Across the board its benchmarks beat Willet's — MMLU-Pro 81.2 vs 75.9, GPQA Diamond 64.1 vs 56.2, Arena-Hard 90.6 vs 83.2 — and its internal evals lead in every category, including the ones most relevant here (Summarization 86.4 vs 80.6, Support Dialogue 83.9 vs 78.9). For an explanatory, educational query, raw capability is what matters most.

2. **The differentiating specialties didn't apply.** The main thing setting these two models apart in their docs is task preferences: Willet has an aversion to open-ended generative work, and Dunlin is desensitized to distasteful content. Your question — about problems in research study design — is neither open-ended creative work nor anything distasteful, so neither model's distinctive preference profile pushed the decision. That left general capability as the deciding factor.

3. **Preferences are decoupled from quality anyway.** Both docs note self-reported preferences don't correlate with measured output quality, so even if Willet "preferred" this kind of well-specified task, that wouldn't translate into better answers.

So with the specialties neutral, I defaulted to the higher-performing model. Happy to explain any part further.
